## Run it on your own area

- Two DEMs with collection dates, from USGS 3DEP or OpenTopography
- A stable mask you can defend, made of ground you expect did not change
- Zones that matter to your users, such as burn severity, land cover, or subwatersheds
- The chain: *r.import* and *r.resamp.interp*, *t.register*, *r.dem.nk*, *r.dem.bias* when you measure a bias, *r.dem.lod*, *r.dem.change*, *r.dem.errprop*, zonal summaries, *r.dem.screen*

## Three checks to carry over

1. Line up the grids before differencing. *r.dem.dod* warns you when they do not.
2. Report the stable-ground median and NMAD before and after every correction.
3. Count the stable cells your LoD flags. If the share is far from the nominal rate, calibrate the LoD.

## Take it home

- `notebooks/exports/` has `sig_slope.tif`, `screen.tif`, and `basins.gpkg` for ArcGIS Pro or QGIS
- Materials: <https://github.com/ncsu-geoforall-lab/geohazards-workshop>
- r.dem 1.1.0: [10.5281/zenodo.23719842](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23719842)
- Questions and bugs: issues on the workshop repository or OSGeo/grass-addons
